sections.title: Character history (Grand Theft Wiki, abridged)
sections.text: Abigail Winthrop, was the assistant of Frank Mathers and in 2009 she married him, after he left his wife. The two remained together but their relationship became strained, mainly due to his environmentalism and his desire to explore the Pacific Ocean surrounding Southern San Andreas. Frank, however, dies when a new submarine began breaking apart after Abigail sabotaged the airlock. She later hires Michael De Santa to explore the ocean floor and retrieve the submarine parts, promising a large reward, which turns out to be $ 10 and an autographed photo of her late husband. Michael suggests to her that the airlock had been tampered with, although she claims that, as an expert in nautical engineering, she can tell it was a malfunction rather than sabotage that caused the submarine to break apart. sections.title: Character history (Grand Theft Wiki, abridged)
sections.text: Sometime in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Michael and Amanda began a relationship. At the time, she worked as a stripper and later a prostitute, with Michael using the gains from his heists to pay for plastic surgery. Eventually, the two get married and have two children: Tracey and Jimmy. Early on, Michael, Amanda, and their children had a seemingly good relationship; however, their relationship became strained in 2004 when Michael arranged for an "off-the-books plea deal" with FIB Agent Dave Norton after a heist gone wrong without consulting her, although he claims that it was to protect her and the children. The family moves to Rockford Hills under Agent Norton's watch. She openly cheats on Michael; however, Michael doesn't initially confront her about it as he cheats on her as well. She eventually became a financial burden on her husband through her shopping, leading Michael to…

sections.title: Trivia (Grand Theft Wiki)
sections.text: She has a profile on www.hushsmush.com, where she lists her age as 43. Amanda was a stripper before she met Michael, according to a story told to Wade by Trevor during their trip to Los Santos. Amanda's habit of cheating on Michael may extend at least as far back as the mid 90s according to dialogue in Reuniting the Family, as Jimmy's third grade teacher is mentioned in a long list of men she is implied to have cheated on Michael with. Reuniting the Family also suggests she slept with the "juice guy", dog walker, garbage collector, Michael's proctologist, Jesse from Vespucci Beach, and at least one other "hippie bum". The license plate of Amanda's Sentinel reads "KRYST4L". Considering she doesn't smoke crystal meth, it can be assumed that this was her stripper name.

sections.title: Character history (Grand Theft Wiki, abridged)
sections.text: Barry is, in 2013, an advocate of legalising marijuana who attempts to convince the people of Los Santos to sign a petition. He meets Michael De Santa and attempts to get him to sign his petition, giving him a joint, which results in Michael thinking he is about to be kidnapped by aliens. During this time Barry continues to argue his case but an angry Michael leaves without signing the petition. Franklin Clinton later meets Barry and agrees to steal two shipments of marijuana. Barry, who had organised a smoke-in with some of his allies, but fails to attend having forgotten with only Franklin showing up outside City Hall. He then meets Trevor Philips who, after smoking a joint, believes he is being attacked by clowns. Trevor, like Michael, also leaves without signing his petition.

sections.title: Character history (Grand Theft Wiki, abridged)
sections.text: Chop is a Rottweiler dog owned by Lamar Davis and lives in Strawberry, Los Santos. The two, according to Lamar, have a 'special bond' due to Lamar's Apache blood. Lamar, on at least one occasion, also gets Chop stoned. In 2013, Chop helps Lamar and Franklin Clinton to locate and kidnap D, a Ballas gangster. When Lamar uses his iFruit phone they are forced to let D go with Lamar later phoning Franklin and asks him to take care of Chop. Chop then moves in with Franklin and his aunt Denise and later accompanies Lamar, Franklin and Trevor Philips to Grove St, although when they are ambushed Chop runs away, returning home. When Franklin moves house to 3671 Whispymound Dr in Vinewood Hills, Chop moves with him rather than going back to Lamar. Chop later accompanies Franklin in helping Trevor to locate Elwood, Walton and Wynn O'Neil, with Chop locating Elwood allowing Franklin to kill him.

sections.title: Mission appearances
sections.text: Chop appears in: Chop; Hood Safari; Predator.

sections.title: Trivia (Grand Theft Wiki)
sections.text: Chop is the first and only playable animal in the series to date. Chop is the first animal to become a protagonist. Chop can be killed by the player, however, he will continue to respawn at Franklin's home. Killing Chop lowers his level of happiness with Franklin. Chop appears on the real-world iFruit app where the player can provide food and water, play with and clean up after him, purchase new collars and teach new tricks. The tricks will then be available in-game, provided Chop is happy with Franklin. Lamar's phone icon is a picture of Chop. A plushie of Chop was made available to win in a Rockstar Games collectible giveaway and later in a Snapmatic screenshot contest.

sections.text: Dave Norton is a corrupt, but fairly reasonable, agent with the Federal Investigation Bureau. Agent Norton was assigned to the case against Michael Townley and Trevor Philips. Prior to the Ludendorff incident in 2004, Agent Norton's career had not been remarkable. During that fateful heist, Norton was at the farm to ambush Michael, Trevor, and their accomplice Brad Snider with a sniper rifle. Norton shoots Michael and Brad while Trevor escaped. sections.text: David Richards was born in 1909 and, at the age of twenty, founded the Richards Majestic film studio in 1929. At an unknown time he married his wife Rachel and had a son named Solomon. He worked extensively with film director Peter Dreyfuss and later allowed his son to become a producer on various films released by the studio, starting with Nelson in Naples in 1968. David and Dreyfuss once took a trip to Mexico and paid two prostitutes to stab each other. David also took film starlet Leonora Johnson under his wing and sent money to her parents Harold and Eileen Johnson. In 1975 Dreyfuss murdered Leonora, which David knew after receiving a confession letter from Dreyfuss, but did not tell the LSPD.
